summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis, was admitted with a three-day history of epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with NPO status, IV hydration, and IV pain and nausea medications. A PICC line was placed for reliable access. CT imaging revealed diffuse colonic thickening concerning for colitis, though C. difficile testing was negative; she was treated with a course of IV antibiotics. She developed hypokalemia due to diarrhea and poor intake, which resolved with supplementation and improved oral intake. She gradually transitioned to oral medications and a regular diet, tolerated her home regimen for over 24 hours, and was discharged home. Lisinopril was held during admission due to low blood pressure and the patient was instructed to discontinue it post-discharge. Follow-up was arranged for colonoscopy and primary care.
